guia.what: Picks a date. An input-style trigger opens a keyboard-navigable calendar (APG pattern). It works with the native `Date` and zero dependencies; month and day names come from `Intl`. The panel lives in the native top layer (Popover API). With `data-ts-range` it picks a span (start and end) in the same calendar, `data-ts-date-preset` adds shortcuts (today, last 7 days, this month) in a column next to the grid, and `data-ts-date-text` lets users type the date in a text field.
whenUse: Capturing a date where seeing the calendar helps people choose (bookings, due dates).
You need a span with a start and end (a deployment window, a billing period). Use `data-ts-range`.
The context of the month or week matters for the decision.
People know the date by heart or paste it from somewhere else (a due date, a ticket). `data-ts-date-text` adds a field to type it in.
Some choices come up again and again (today, the last 7 days, this month). Add them as shortcuts with `data-ts-date-preset`.
You need to restrict it to a range (`data-ts-min`/`data-ts-max`) or respect a locale (`data-ts-locale`).
You want the complete field, with a label, hint, and error.
Some days can’t be picked (weekends, holidays, a custom rule), or should be flagged with a mark (meetings, deployments).
whenAvoid: The date is known and typing is faster (a date of birth) → a formatted `input`.
It’s only a time, with no date, or a value that isn’t a date → the matching control.
dos: Use `data-ts-min`/`data-ts-max` to restrict it to valid dates, and `data-ts-disabled-weekdays`, `data-ts-disabled-dates`, or `setDatePickerDisabledDate` for individual days that can’t be picked.
Use `data-ts-day-marks` to flag events with a dot and a short label. Screen readers announce the label, and it’s also used as the `title`.
Call `setDatePickerLoading(root, true)` while you fetch marks or unavailable days from the server. It doesn’t block the field.
Build it with the `field` markup for forms, or keep its label, hint, and error next to the field when it stands alone. Make the expected format clear.
In the typeable field (`data-ts-date-text`), use `readonly`, not `disabled`, to show a date that can’t be edited. It stays focusable and reads better.
For relative shortcuts, use the keys (`today`, `last-7-days`, `last-30-days`, `this-week`, `this-month`, `last-month`). They’re resolved on click, not when the page is built.
With `data-ts-range` inside a form, put a `name` on both `<input type="hidden">` elements (`data-ts-date-input="start"` and `"end"`). Two `yyyy-mm-dd` dates are submitted, start and end.
donts: Don’t make people page through months to reach a distant date they already know.
Don’t turn on `data-ts-date-text` if people only choose among a few dates on the calendar. An editable field invites typos that the calendar avoids.
Don’t expect `ts:change` on the first click of a range. It only fires once the range is complete or cleared.
Don’t pass a range key to a single-date calendar (or `today` as a multi-day range). It isn’t drawn, and you get a warning in development.
Don’t assume a format. Respect the user’s locale.
Don’t rely on the mark’s color alone. Always write its `label`.

teclado.action: Moves the focused day (by day and by week). In RTL, the grid is mirrored: ← moves forward one day and → moves back.
First and last day of the week.
Previous and next month. If the day doesn’t exist in that month, it lands on the last day.
Selects the focused day, closes the calendar, and returns focus to the trigger.

The first press sets the start, and the calendar stays open. The arrow keys move the range preview. The second press sets the end, closes, and returns focus to the trigger. Esc halfway through discards the start.

With presets (`data-ts-date-preset`), Tab goes through the presets first (a column at the start of the panel) and then the calendar. On open, focus stays on the day. Enter, Space, or a click on a preset confirms the value, closes the panel, and returns focus to the trigger.

With the typeable field, clicking or tabbing into it doesn’t open the calendar (the calendar button is a separate tab stop, after the field). Enter or leaving the field confirms what was typed. If it’s unreadable, nonexistent, outside the allowed range, or an unavailable day, the text reverts to the last valid value, and an empty field clears the date. Inside a `<form>`, Enter lets the submission go through. In range mode, Tab moves from the start field to the end field without confirming. The pair is confirmed when focus leaves the group.
Opens the calendar with focus on the focusable day (the selected one or, with no value, today). Esc closes it and returns focus to the trigger.

nucleo: It’s its own calendar with keyboard navigation. The native `<input>` only provides the text field. Draws the calendar grid, handles keyboard navigation, and formats the date. With a trigger it’s fully functional, with the calendar in a panel that opens, closes, and returns focus. Each day’s accessible name is the full date. If the attributes below change through JavaScript, the calendar redraws.
